- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction starting from day 10–15 of forecast horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 2–3% bias upward for such cases.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; extend upward bias by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag; apply 1–2 day lag correction by shifting forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day.
